items.q: Which multi-protein complex of the mitochondrial electron transport chain does NOT pump protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane into the intermembrane space?
items.exp: Complexes I, III, and IV pump protons outward into the intermembrane space (4, 4, and 2 protons per electron pair, respectively). Complex II transfers electrons from FADH2 to ubiquinone without pumping any protons.
r: Correct. Complex II does not pump protons across the inner mitochondrial membrane.
Incorrect. Complex I pumps 4 protons per electron pair.
Incorrect. Complex III pumps 4 protons per electron pair via the Q-cycle.
Incorrect. Complex IV pumps 2 protons per electron pair.
items.kp: Complex II (succinate dehydrogenase) transfers electrons from FADH2 to ubiquinone without pumping protons, yielding fewer ATP per FADH2 than NADH.

items.q: A patient presents with acute collapse, metabolic lactic acidosis, and a venous oxygen saturation of 92% after inhaling smoke from burning plastic. Cyanide poisoning is suspected. Which enzyme is inhibited by cyanide binding?
items.exp: Cyanide binds tightly to ferric iron (Fe3+) in heme a3 of cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV), blocking the terminal reduction of oxygen to water, which arrests electron transport and causes cellular hypoxia with high venous PO2.
r: Correct. Cyanide inhibits Complex IV by binding ferric heme a3.
Incorrect. Rotenone inhibits Complex I.
Incorrect. Oligomycin inhibits Complex V.
Incorrect. Arsenic inhibits pyruvate dehydrogenase.
items.kp: Cyanide inhibits cytochrome c oxidase (Complex IV), blocking oxygen reduction and causing severe cellular histotoxic hypoxia with high venous oxygen saturation.

items.q: How does 2,4-dinitrophenol (DNP) uncouple mitochondrial oxidative phosphorylation, and what clinical manifestation is characteristic of overdose?
o: Transports protons across the inner membrane collapsing the proton gradient; causes lethal hyperpyrexia and diaphoresis
Inhibits Complex I, causing hypothermia and bradycardia
Directly binds ATP synthase, stopping electron transport
Inhibits cytochrome c oxidase, causing cyanosis
items.exp: DNP is a lipophilic weak acid that picks up protons in the intermembrane space and diffuses across the inner membrane, discharging the proton gradient without ATP generation. Energy is released entirely as heat, causing severe hyperpyrexia.
r: Correct. DNP collapses the proton gradient, producing uncontrolled thermogenesis and hyperpyrexia.
Incorrect. Complex I inhibition does not cause hyperpyrexia.
Incorrect. Oligomycin binds ATP synthase, but it is an inhibitor, not an uncoupler.
Incorrect. DNP does not inhibit Complex IV.

items.q: Oligomycin halts mitochondrial respiration in vitro by binding to which subunit of ATP synthase, blocking proton translocation back into the matrix?
items.exp: Oligomycin binds to the c-subunit of the hydrophobic F0 domain in the inner membrane, blocking the proton channel. Without proton flow, F1 rotation stops, halting both ATP synthesis and electron transport in coupled mitochondria.
r: Correct. Oligomycin inhibits the F0 proton channel of ATP synthase.
Incorrect. Aurovertin inhibits the F1 headpiece.
Incorrect. Gamma stalk rotates inside F1.
Incorrect. Delta stalk anchors F1 to F0.
items.kp: Oligomycin inhibits the F0 proton channel of ATP synthase (Complex V), arresting both ATP synthesis and coupled electron transport.

items.q: What is the physiological function of uncoupling protein 1 (UCP1 / thermogenin) localized in the inner mitochondrial membrane of brown adipose tissue?
o: Provides a regulated proton leak into the matrix to generate heat for non-shivering thermogenesis
Pumps protons outward to maximize ATP synthesis
Exports fatty acids from brown fat into plasma
Converts white adipose tissue into skeletal muscle
items.exp: Thermogenin (UCP1) is an endogenous proton channel in brown adipocytes. Activated by free fatty acids under norepinephrine stimulation, it dissipates the proton gradient to produce heat for non-shivering thermogenesis in neonates.
r: Correct. UCP1 dissipates the proton gradient into the matrix to produce heat.
Incorrect. It does not pump protons outward.
Incorrect. It does not export fatty acids.
Incorrect. It is expressed in brown and beige fat, not muscle.

items.q: Which specific chemical compound selectively inhibits electron transport at Complex III (cytochrome bc1 complex) by binding to the Qi site?
items.exp: Antimycin A inhibits Complex III (cytochrome bc1) by blocking the Qi quinone reduction site, preventing electron transfer from heme bH to ubiquinone.
r: Correct. Antimycin A inhibits Complex III at the Qi site.
Incorrect. Rotenone inhibits Complex I.
Incorrect. Cyanide inhibits Complex IV.
Incorrect. Carbon monoxide inhibits Complex IV.

items.q: Carbon monoxide inhibits cellular respiration by competing with oxygen for binding to reduced heme a3 in which respiratory complex?
items.exp: Carbon monoxide competes with molecular oxygen for binding to the reduced ferrous (Fe2+) heme a3-CuB binuclear center of Complex IV, inhibiting mitochondrial respiration alongside its carboxyhemoglobin effect.
r: Correct. CO inhibits Complex IV by competing with oxygen at heme a3.
Incorrect. Complex I does not contain heme a3.
Incorrect. Complex II transfers electrons from FAD to ubiquinone.
Incorrect. Complex III contains hemes b and c1.

items.q: Rotenone, a natural botanical compound previously used as a pesticide, potently blocks mitochondrial respiration by inhibiting electron transfer in which complex?
items.exp: Rotenone (and piericidin A) inhibits Complex I by binding the ubiquinone reduction site, blocking electron transfer from iron-sulfur cluster N2 to coenzyme Q.
r: Correct. Rotenone inhibits Complex I.
Incorrect. Complex II is inhibited by malonate.
Incorrect. Complex III is inhibited by antimycin A.
Incorrect. Complex IV is inhibited by cyanide and azide.

items.q: Which mobile electron carrier shuttles electrons between Complex III and Complex IV along the outer surface of the inner mitochondrial membrane?
items.exp: Cytochrome c is a small, water-soluble peripheral membrane hemoprotein that shuttles electrons one at a time from Complex III (cytochrome c1) to Complex IV (CuA site) in the intermembrane space.
r: Correct. Cytochrome c is the mobile peripheral carrier shuttling electrons from Complex III to IV.
Incorrect. Coenzyme Q is a lipid-soluble quinone shuttling from Complexes I/II to III.
Incorrect. FAD is an enzyme-bound prosthetic group.
Incorrect. NADH donates electrons to Complex I.

items.q: Atractyloside is a toxic plant glycoside that arrests mitochondrial ATP synthesis. What transport mechanism does atractyloside inhibit?
items.exp: Atractyloside (and bongkrekic acid) inhibits the adenine nucleotide translocase (ANT) in the inner mitochondrial membrane, stopping export of newly made ATP into cytosol and import of ADP for phosphorylation.
r: Correct. Atractyloside inhibits the adenine nucleotide translocase (ANT).
Incorrect. The phosphate carrier transports Pi.
Incorrect. VDAC is on the outer membrane.
Incorrect. The pyruvate carrier transports pyruvate into matrix.
